scope: Proposition 10.16 (Exponential occupancy bound) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 120. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Put β = 1/2+d2 > 1. Assume the fixed-code test of Proposition 10.15 in the following quantitative form: for every sufficiently small ζ > 0, choose a fixed boundary tolerance sufficiently small and a fixed R sufficiently large so that, once the minimum radius is sufficiently large, every favorable admissible decorated code c satisfies P{c is realized} ≤ exp   −βλE(c) + ζλT(c) + CR,ζM(c) . (10.24) This estimate is required uniformly in the fixed displacement U. The realization event includes all the actual marked chord constraints. The fractional boundary deletions are absorbed into the ζλT term, and the structural deletions into the explicit terminal term, using the bounded number of sorted-chain charges at each deleted vertex. The fixed-code estimate includes its oscillation exceptions. No such estimate is asserted here for codes whose slots are predominantly irregular. Then there are C, c, C1 > 0, independent of any fixed finite exploration cutoff, such that for all sufficiently large N and all u ≥ 0, P{A ≥ CN + u} ≤ C1 exp(−cN − cu). (10.25) The estimate holds for any word-dependent selection of witness lists made before U. It also holds for a fixed reference grid, and with A replaced by its maximum over grid displacements. The threshold in “sufficiently large” may depend on the fixed exploration cutoff. If Equation (10.8) holds, then EQN A = O(N). (10.26) The corresponding code has length at most a deterministic constant times N with QN -probability tending to one. At an independently and uniformly sampled level j ∈ {0, . . . , J}, EQN mj = O(1).
